darwin.fallback_note: the vendor's backend is 'keychain-with-plaintext-fallback': when the Keychain refuses a write (locked over SSH) the login goes to the same file Linux uses, and is read from there whenever the Keychain holds nothing

enabled_by.note: Credential Manager is a staged rollout, off unless the vendor's cached feature flag or the environment variable says otherwise. With it off the login is the plain file, exactly as on Linux, and the vendor never reads Credential Manager

secure_dir.note: where the credentials FILE lives: this variable when set (the default directory when set but empty), otherwise the config directory

liveness.optional_note: absent from credentials written by the VS Code extension bundle; a missing value means UNKNOWN, never CLOSED

config_file.name: .claude{suffix}.json
config_file.note: Claude Code 2.1.300: the global config is $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.claude{suffix}.json when that variable is set and ~/.claude{suffix}.json when not. A legacy .config.json inside the config directory wins when it is a file and either holds something or is writable while the new file does not exist yet.

identity.account_note: one address can belong to several organisations (a subscription and a Team or Console seat), each a separate login; a known mismatch is drift
identity.plan_note: NOT claudeAiOauth.subscriptionType, which read 'team' for a Max 5x account

companion.note: keys absent from the incoming profile are deleted, not left holding the previous account's identity
companion.stale_note: cachedUsageUtilization is stashed so a parked profile's card can show its last known figures, but never written back: a cache restored from a switch describes whatever the account was doing days ago and reads as current.

policy.rotates_note: the refresh token is replaced on every refresh: the client stores whatever refresh_token the server returns (2.1.300, keeping the old one only if none is returned), and on 2026-11-13 a real refresh returned a new one. A stash taken before a refresh holds a spent token, so the active profile is re-stashed after use, as Codex's is -- on proof of lineage only, never on the address in the config file.
policy.warn_days_note: the measured refresh window is roughly four days, so a threshold of seven would render every profile amber permanently

login.hint: Run 'claude auth login' in a terminal.
login.note: claude auth login opens the browser and runs its own callback server. --email pre-populates the address on the login page.

provenance.executed_how: the real-machine workflow on GitHub-hosted runners, with made-up credentials and the vendor's own status command as judge: macOS 15 and 26 arm64, macOS 15 x86_64, Windows Server 2022 and 2025 x64, Windows 11 arm64, Ubuntu 22.04 x64 and 24.04 arm64. No real account was used on any of them
provenance.source: the store layout was read out of the 2.1.322 binaries for win32-x64 and darwin-arm64 (npm @anthropic-ai/claude-code-*), and the Windows target-name mapping out of oven-sh/bun src/jsc/bindings/SecretsWindows.cpp

surfaces_note: one switch moves both — they share one credential store, so a shell must show them together or 'why did VS Code change too' needs explaining

lineage.note: the sign-in deadline. It does not roll: the server keeps one absolute deadline, about 30 days after sign-in, and returns the seconds left on every refresh, which Claude Code adds to its own clock. So the stored value wobbles by rounding and network delay (-1.375 s across an 8-hour refresh, measured 2026-11-13) while the deadline holds. Two credentials whose deadlines agree within tolerance_ms (10 s, against a measured wobble of 1.4 s) are one login, refreshed. Two sign-ins less than ten seconds apart are the one case it cannot tell apart; a deadline that moved further (network delay, a clock that jumped) is read as another login, which costs a backup, never a login.

token.note: emptied in place when the login is cleared; the expiry and scopes around it survive, so a credential with no token still reads as healthy unless this is checked
